extracted.intended_audience: general literary readers, poets, and students of literature
extracted.subtask_description: Close reading and extraction of evaluative principles embedded in Ralph Waldo Emerson's essay (sections on Imagination, Art, and Experience). The content is literary-philosophical guidance about imagination, poetry, art, and living.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative metamorphosis / tropes as liberation
rubrics_metrics.description: The metamorphosis excites in the beholder an emotion of joy. The use of symbols has a certain power of emancipation and exhilaration for all men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols, tropes, fables, oracles and poetic forms give readers a new sense and reveal 'another world' inside our world; this initial imaginative stimulation is of prime value even before precise sense is extracted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of the transcendental and extraordinary in books
rubrics_metrics.description: I think nothing is of any value in books excepting the transcendental and extraordinary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that depart from routine—even those containing questionable facts or strange cosmogonies (e.g., Pythagoras, Swedenborg)—are valuable as 'certificates of departure' from routine and as witnesses of new thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of imaginative stimulation over literal precision
rubrics_metrics.description: An imaginative book renders us much more service at first, by stimulating us through its tropes, than afterward when we arrive at the precise sense of the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial emotional and imaginative effect of a work (its tropes and metamorphoses) is more important than later analytical 'precise sense'; poetic value often lies in the first imaginative unlocking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep symbols fluxional — avoid fixing accidental symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the imagination is to flow, and not to freeze... Mysticism consists in the mistake of an accidental and individual symbol for an universal one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should not nail a symbol to one sense or make a personal/accidental image serve as a universal standard; symbols must be willing to be translated into terms significant to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer universal signs over local/village symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us have a little algebra, instead of this trite rhetoric,—universal signs, instead of these village symbols,—and we shall both be gainers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, employ broader, more universally translatable imagery or concepts ('algebra' / universal signs) rather than idiosyncratic, private metaphors that fail to convey to other minds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality as emancipation — introduce new thought
rubrics_metrics.description: He unlocks our chains and admits us to a new scene. The poet or inventor who yields us a new thought is a measure of intellect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The highest praise is reserved for those who depart from routine and present genuinely new visions or thoughts that free the reader's mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic aim: symmetry and abundance of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is the path of the creator to his work... all partake one desire, namely to express themselves symmetrically and abundantly, not dwarfishly and fragmentarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good art strives for comprehensive, balanced, and ample expression rather than narrow, cramped, or fragmentary treatment of its subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursuit of the half-seen beauty (creative striving)
rubrics_metrics.description: He pursues a beauty, half seen, which flies before him... by and by he says something which is original and beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mark of creative work is the persistent pursuit of an elusive perception of beauty; the artist's continuing chase eventually yields original and beautiful utterances amid much convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence and inner necessity in creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Doubt not, O poet, but persist. Say 'It is in me, and shall out.' Stand there, balked and dumb... stand and strive, until at last rage draw out of thee that dream-power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True artistic production requires dogged persistence and obedience to an internal compulsion; perseverance is a criterion of authentic creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and inexhaustibility as marks of greatness
rubrics_metrics.description: His genius is no longer exhaustible. All the creatures by pairs and by tribes pour into his mind... the rich poets... have obviously no limits to their works except the limits of their lifetime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great artists possess a depth and abundance of vision that enable prolific, varied, and seemingly limitless creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renunciation and dedication to the muse
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt leave the world, and know the muse only... Thou shalt lie close hid with nature, and canst not be afforded to the Capitol or the Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A true artist accepts social renunciations and apprenticeships—seclusion, simplicity, and devotion to nature and the muse—as a condition of producing authentic work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address life plainly and profoundly; sing the times
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not with sufficient plainness or sufficient profoundness address ourselves to life, nor dare we chaunt our own times and social circumstance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poets should engage candidly and deeply with contemporary life, social conditions, and national materials rather than only classical or remote themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of national/local material as valid poetic subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks and tariffs, the newspaper and caucus, Methodism and Unitarianism... are yet unsung. Yet America is a poem in our eyes; its ample geography dazzles the imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local, national, and ordinary materials (politics, commerce, regional life) are legitimate poetic raw material and can yield large imaginative results if treated rightly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art of life: fill the hour — practical wisdom over chronic criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: To fill the hour,—that is happiness; to fill the hour and leave no crevice for a repentance or an approval... The true art of life is to skate well on [surfaces].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond artistic criteria, Emerson prescribes a practical standard for living: attend to and complete the present moment, balancing thought with sturdy action rather than perpetual critical postponement.
